The Recursive Agents Hackathon
Shack15, San Francisco, CASat, Oct 17 at 9:00 AM – 10:00 PM (PDT)

Build a team of agents you can walk away from.

During the PyTorch Conference in San Francisco, build agents that can take a goal and run with it. Let them make the plan, spin up sub-agents, delegate work, communicate with each other, check their own progress, recover when things break, and keep going.

Push beyond the one-shot agent into persistent loops that rarely need you involved: agents building teams and handling delegation, memory, and long-running inference that can keep operating after you walk away until the work is complete

Build on Crusoe Managed Inference and put leading open models, including NVIDIA’s Nemotron family, into production on high-performance NVIDIA infrastructure.

Compete to win $25,000 in cash prizes and an NVIDIA RTX 5090.

Note: This event is fully in-person in San Francisco. Teams may have up to four members. All attendees must apply and be approved to attend.

About Event

​Agentic AI Hackathon at AWS Community Day Bay Area 2026

​Build an agent that does real work on AWS. Two weeks. One track. Eight teams demo live on stage at AWS Community Day in front of 500+ builders. Up to $3,200 in AWS credits for the winners. First 25 teams to be formed will each get $50 AWS credits to build their ideas and bring it to life.

​How it works

​Register here by September 30. Every team member registers individually on this page and enters the same team name.

​Build from October 1 to October 11 remotely. The top 8 submissions get a 5-minute live demo slot on October 13 at the AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco, judged on the spot, with winners announced at the closing session.

​Who should join

​Anyone building with Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents SDK, SageMaker, or any other AWS AI service. Teams of 2 to 4. Solo builders welcome; register anyway and we'll match you with a team before September 29.

​The rules in brief

​Work starts September 29, not before

​At least two AWS services, one of them an AI service

​Public GitHub repo, MIT or Apache 2.0 license

​No production data, PHI, or PII

​You keep your IP

​Submit by October 11, 11:59 AM PT: public repo, 3-minute demo video, one-page writeup. Submission link goes out in the October 1 start announcement.

​Judging: technical depth (30%), real-world usefulness (25%), responsible AI (20%), demo and communication (15%), completeness (10%). Judges score all submissions asynchronously on October 12, then re-score the 8 finalists live.

​Prizes: 1st place gets $500 in AWS credits per team member (up to 4). 2nd place gets $300 per team member (up to 4). All 8 finalists get their demo featured on the AWS Community Bay Area YouTube channel.

​Full participant guide: https://www.aws-aicd.com/hackathon/

​Questions: Post in the Event Chat (you're added when you register) or use Contact the Host/ hello@shravanthv.com for anything private. Reply target is 24 hours.

​You must also be registered for AWS Community Day at https://events.builder.aws.com/mevA9Z and present in person on October 13.

​Hosted by AWS User Group Bay Area.

candidates.evidence:
AboutHackathonAgendaSpeakersVenueSponsorsVolunteersFAQContactRegister
AboutHackathonAgendaSpeakersVenueSponsorsVolunteersFAQContactRegister for free

October 13, 2026 · AWS Builder Loft

← AWS Community Day 2026

Agentic AI Hackathon

Participant Guide

Build an agent that does real work on AWS.

Two weeks. One track. Eight teams demo live on stage at AWS Community Day in front of 200+ builders. Up to $3,200 in AWS credits on the line.

Build window: Tuesday, September 29 to Tuesday, October 13, 2026
Finals: AWS Community Day, AI Edition, October 13, 2026, AWS Builder Loft, 525 Market St, Floor 2, San Francisco, CA 94105
Register by: Monday, September 28
Register: on the Luma event page. Fill in the registration questions; that is your team sign-up.
Questions: Post in the Luma Event Chat (you are added automatically when you register) so everyone benefits from the answer, or use Contact the Host on the Luma page for anything private. No calls or office hours. Reply target is 24 hours.
What you'll build

Any agentic AI application on AWS. Think agents that plan, call tools, remember context, and complete a task a real person cares about. Projects for accessibility, healthcare, education, or public good are welcome and tend to score well on usefulness, but everyone competes in one pool.

Two weeks is enough for a working prototype, not a finished product. Judges know that. Scope accordingly.

Who can join
Teams of 2 to 4 people.
Flying solo? Register anyway and answer yes to "match me" in the Luma registration questions. The lead will connect you with other solo builders in the Event Chat before September 29.
You must be registered for AWS Community Day. Finalists present in person.
Organizers, judges, and their immediate work teammates can't win prizes.
Not registered for Community Day yet? Register here, it is free.
Rules
All hackathon work starts on or after September 29, when the start announcement goes out on Luma. Open-source libraries and frameworks are fine. Renaming an existing project is not.
Use at least two AWS services, and at least one must be an AI service: Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, SageMaker, Strands Agents SDK, Amazon Q, Transcribe, Rekognition, and similar all count.
Your code must be in a public GitHub repo. Private repos, invite-only links, and zip files will not be accepted. The repo must be public at the time you submit and stay public through October 13. License it MIT or Apache 2.0.
No production customer data, PHI, or PII. Use synthetic or public datasets.
You own your IP. We just want to see it.
Be kind. The event code of conduct applies to every channel and the day itself.
Timeline
Date	What happensNow through Mon Sep 28	Register your team.
Tue Sep 29	Hackathon starts. Start announcement goes out on Luma (email blast and Event Chat) with the final rules, rubric, writeup template, submission form, and any AWS credit details. Build begins.
Sep 29 to Oct 11	Build. Questions go in the Luma Event Chat.
Sun Oct 11, 11:59 PM PT	Submissions due. No extensions.
Mon Oct 12 by 6 PM PT	Finalists notified by email.
Tue Oct 13	Community Day. Finalists check in at the hackathon room, dry-run on the main stage over lunch, demo live at 4:15 PM after the closing remarks. Winners announced right after the last demo.
How to submit

By Sunday, October 11, 11:59 PM PT, submit via the submission form (link goes live September 29 with the start announcement):

Public GitHub repo with a README covering what it does and how to run it. We will open the link while logged out; if it 404s, the submission doesn't count.
3-minute demo video (YouTube unlisted or Loom). This is your backup if the live demo fails, so make it good.
One-page writeup using the template: the problem, who it helps, an architecture diagram, AWS services used, and what you'd build next.
Team roster with each member's name and email. This is what we use to issue credits, so get it right.

Download the writeup template (Word) → Fill in every section, keep it to one page, and export it as a PDF for the submission form.

How you'll be judged

Every criterion is scored 1 to 5 by each judge.

Technical depth

30%

A 5 looks like: Real agentic behavior (planning, tool use, memory), sound AWS architecture, more than a prompt wrapper

Real-world usefulness

25%

A 5 looks like: Solves a problem a real user has, clear target user, plausible path to adoption

Responsible AI

20%

A 5 looks like: Guardrails, handles failure and hallucination, considers privacy and misuse, cites data sources

Demo and communication

15%

A 5 looks like: Works live, tells a clear story, honest about limitations

Completeness and polish

10%

A 5 looks like: Runs from the README, has tests or evals, clean repo

Round 1 (Oct 12): Judges score every submission from your video, repo, and writeup. The top 8 become finalists.

Round 2 (Oct 13): Finalists demo live. You get 5 minutes, hard stop, with a visible timer. Judges may ask a quick question or two in the 1-minute changeover. Final score is 40% Round 1 and 60% live demo.

Judges decide right after the eighth demo and the winners are announced on stage before the room empties, around 5:00 PM.

Prizes
Winning team: $2,000 in AWS credits ($500 per member, up to 4 members)
Runner-up team: $1,200 in AWS credits ($300 per member, up to 4 members)

All 8 finalists get their demo recorded and featured on the AWS Community Bay Area YouTube channel, plus a shout-out from the organizers on LinkedIn.

Credits are AWS promotional credits applied to your own AWS account, issued within about two weeks after the event. Make sure every team member has an AWS account in their own name. Promotional credits typically have an expiry date and some service restrictions; we'll share the exact terms when codes are issued.

Finalist day-of checklist (Oct 13)
Arrive when doors open at 9:30 AM and check in at the hackathon room (the Track B room, yours until 2:00 PM).
Do the mandatory dry run with a volunteer on the main stage during lunch, 1:00 to 2:00 PM. Every team, no exceptions.
Bring your own laptop, charger, and any adapters. We'll have HDMI and USB-C at the stage.
Have your backup video open in a tab.
Practice the 5-minute version. Then practice the 4-minute version.
Tips from the organizers
Pick the demo moment first, then build backward from it.
A narrow agent that reliably does one thing beats a broad agent that sometimes does five.
Show the failure handling. Judges love seeing what happens when the tool call errors out.
Ask early. Nobody has ever regretted posting a question in the chat on October 3 instead of discovering the problem on October 11.

See you on stage October 13.

Hackathon lead: Shravanth Venkatesh, AWS User Group Leader, Bay Area

About Event

​NOTE: By registering for the Luma, you are submitting an application to participate. We will reach out on a rolling basis to let you know whether you've been accepted. There are a limited number of devices, we can support up to 200 participants.

​This event is sponsored by Meta, Qualcomm, GitHub, Open Intelligence Foundation, and the PyTorch Foundation.

​Join developers, researchers, and builders for the upcoming ExecuTorch Hackathon on October 17 -18 at Founder’s Inc., officially part of Open Source AI Week 2026.

​Hosted in collaboration with Qualcomm, Meta, GitHub, the PyTorch Foundation, and Open Intelligence Foundation, this hands-on event will challenge teams to build innovative AI experiences powered by ExecuTorch—an open-source framework for deploying and running PyTorch models efficiently on edge and on-device hardware.

​Participants will work in teams of 3–5 people and select one of three tracks outlined below. Each team will receive a device from their selected track to use during the event. Builders will also get access to GitHub Copilot Pro+ to support their builds.

​Compute Track

​Build AI applications optimized for the Copilot+ PC powered by Snapdragon® X Elite processors, exploring the potential of powerful, efficient on-device AI computing.

​Mobile + XR Track

​Create AI-powered experiences for the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite and Samsung Galaxy XR powered by Snapdragon® XR2+ Gen 2 processor, with a focus on mobile intelligence, immersive interaction, and multimodal applications.

​IoT Track

​Develop intelligent edge and embedded applications using the Arduino® VENTUNO™ Q boards, combining on-device AI with real-time sensing, control, and connected experiences. Choose from an assortment of modulinos and accessories to complete your project (available on a first come, first served basis).

​To participate, interested teams must select a track, form a team of 3–5, and submit a project proposal by October 4. Selected teams will be announced by October 7.

​Prizes

​The top team in each track will receive a prize package for every member of the team: Meta AI glasses and an Arduino® UNO™ Q. Build a standout project, demonstrate the potential of on-device AI, and take home hardware to continue exploring the edge.

GitHub will also award a one-year subscription to Copilot Pro to the winner.

​Whether you are an experienced edge AI developer or eager to explore the future of open-source, on-device intelligence, the ExecuTorch Hackathon is an opportunity to collaborate, experiment, and build with the latest hardware and software across compute, mobile, XR, and IoT.

​Questions? Join our Discord!
Ask questions about the event, connect with other participants, form a team, receive event announcements, and stay up to date throughout the hackathon.

​👉 Join here: Join Discord Server

​Bring your ideas. Build with ExecuTorch. Help shape the future of open-source, on device AI.

​

​About Open Intelligence Foundation

​The Open Intelligence Foundation is a community-first nonprofit founded to protect, strengthen, and advance open-source AI, open models, and open science. Supported by a large community of volunteers and organizations, it takes a bottom-up approach to collaboration, working with academia and researchers to support research, development, and education in open-source AI. The foundation also leads Open Source AI Week, a community-run initiative celebrating open-source AI.

​About Founders, Inc.
Founders, Inc. backs early-stage founders in emerging tech with first checks and 55,000 sq. ft. of lab space in San Francisco's Fort Mason. They run year-round programs to help ambitious builders to go from early stage to scalable companies.

​

​Snapdragon and Qualcomm branded products are products of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. and/or its subsidiaries. Arduino and VENTUNO are trademarks or registered trademarks of Arduino S.r.l.

About Event
​The Builder Base: Buildathon

​Your idea. Your stack. Your build.

​Welcome to The Builder Base: Buildathon — a one-day gathering in San Francisco for engineers, AI builders, founders, designers, and technology professionals who want to spend a full day turning ideas into working products.

​Builder Base is built around one simple idea: give builders the space, tools, people, and time to build.

​Whether you're experimenting with an AI agent, launching a developer tool, creating an enterprise workflow, building a data product, automating a painful process, or working on something completely unconventional, this is your base for the day.

​Come with an idea, a problem, a technology you want to explore — or nothing more than the desire to build. Find teammates, get feedback from experienced builders, learn from industry experts, and ship something you're proud of.

​Event Details

​When: 9:30 AM – 7:00 PM, 30 October 2026
Where: San Francisco, CA
Format: One-day, in-person buildathon
Who: Engineers, AI Builders, Founders, Product Managers, Designers, Data Scientists, and Technology Professionals
Theme: Open-ended — Build what matters

​What to Expect

​A full day dedicated to building

​Turn an idea into a functional prototype

​Collaborate with engineers, founders, designers, and AI practitioners

​Meet potential teammates and future collaborators

​Mentorship and guidance from experienced industry professionals

​Access to modern AI tools, APIs, platforms, and developer resources

​Partner credits, challenges, and special prizes

​Live product demos and project showcases

​Networking with San Francisco's technology and startup community

​Food, refreshments, swag, and prizes

​What Can You Build?

​Anything worth building.

​Build an AI application, autonomous agent, developer tool, enterprise workflow, data platform, automation system, productivity tool, consumer product, infrastructure project, or an idea nobody has tried before.

​There are no prescribed problem statements and no requirement to build around a particular technology.

​Find a problem. Build the solution. Ship it.

​You can arrive with a fully formed idea or figure it out once you get there. The goal is to spend the day building, experimenting, learning, and turning an idea into something real.

​Who Should Join?

​The Builder Base is for people who make things.

​Whether you're an experienced software engineer, an AI developer exploring agentic systems, a founder testing a new idea, a product manager turning a concept into a prototype, a designer bringing an experience to life, or a student and early-career developer looking for your next challenge — you're welcome.

​You don't need to be an expert. You just need to be ready to build.

​Come with an idea. Leave with a build.

Open-weight models now serve roughly a third of all tokens in an increasingly fragmented ecosystem
Creative roleplay is the dominant open-source use case

About Event
​Women Build Oakland: From Idea to App in One Day

​Have an idea for an app, website, or digital tool—but not sure how to build it?

​Women Build Oakland is a free, beginner-friendly AI buildathon designed to help women turn ideas into working digital products in just one day.

​Presented by CoCo Noir Labs, this hands-on event will bring together 50 women founders, professionals, creatives, students, small-business owners, community leaders, and aspiring technology builders.

​No previous coding experience is required.

​Participants will join small teams of two to four women and work together to build one shared app, website, or digital tool that addresses a real business or community challenge. You can contribute through business strategy, research, project management, design, marketing, storytelling, prompting, testing, coding, or presenting.

​What to Expect

​During the event, participants will:

​Learn the basics of AI-powered vibe coding

​See how an idea can become a working digital product

​Meet women with different professional and creative skills

​Form a team around a shared idea or challenge

​Build a functional prototype with support from mentors

​Present the completed project to a panel of judges

​Compete for prizes and special recognition

​Teams may build solutions related to:

​Women’s economic opportunity and entrepreneurship

​Small-business and hospitality innovation

​Health, wellness, caregiving, and safety

​Workforce development and education

​Community and public services

​Oakland’s culture and creative economy

​Who Should Apply

​This event is for women and women-identifying adults who are curious about AI, technology, entrepreneurship, or solving meaningful problems.

​You may be a:

​First-time AI builder

​Founder or small-business owner

​Working professional or executive

​Creative or community leader

​Student or career changer

​Designer, product manager, or developer

​Beginners are encouraged to apply. You do not need to arrive with an idea or have technical experience. You only need to be ready to learn, collaborate, and build.

​Registration Details

​Participation is free

​Space is limited to 50 builders

​Registration is application-based

​Submitting an application does not guarantee acceptance

​Accepted participants must be available for the full program from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

​Participants should bring a laptop and charger

​Lunch, refreshments, mentorship, and event materials will be provided

​Come with an idea or simply come ready to collaborate. By the end of the day, you will have helped create a real digital product and gained the confidence to continue building with AI.

​Presented and produced by CoCo Noir Labs

​The event is designed to use Lovable as the primary AI app-building platform, subject to approval through Lovable’s Community Events program.

​This event has been submitted for inclusion in Oakland Tech Week 2026 and is pending final confirmation.

Space is limited and is mandatory to register on https://events.builder.aws.com/EARgN9 (required to enter the AWS building) and join the discord: https://discord.gg/QF2AkaAfTr
All guests must be 18+ and present a valid government-issued physical photo ID at check-in (digital IDs will not be accepted). Scooters and bikes are not permitted in any Amazon building with no on-site parking available.

The Universal Celebration Hackathon is a celebration of creativity, entrepreneurship, and the next generation of AI-powered companies. Bring your ideas, experiment with new possibilities, and turn your vision into something real.
This hackathon is about more than building a prototype. It’s about imagining what a company looks like when AI agents can work together as a team.
The Challenge
Build a company run by a team of AI agents.
Your challenge is to create an AI-native business or startup where multiple specialized agents work together to build, operate, and grow the company.
Think of your agents as your founding team. You might have a CEO agent defining strategy, a product agent building the product, engineering agents writing code, marketing agents finding customers, sales agents closing deals, finance agents managing the business, and operations or customer-support agents keeping everything running.
The key question is:
What happens when you give an AI team a business to run?

What to Build
Build a working prototype of a company powered by a team of collaborating AI agents.
Your project should:
Identify a real problem or opportunity.
Define a clear product, service, or business.
Create multiple AI agents with distinct roles and responsibilities.
Show how your agents communicate, collaborate, and make decisions.
Demonstrate how the agents can actually execute business tasks.
Show how your company could acquire customers, deliver value, and grow.
You can build for consumers, businesses, creators, communities, or any other audience.
Don’t just build an AI feature. Build the beginnings of an AI-native company.
Tracks
Choose one or multiple tracks and build your company within them.
Climate, Sustainability & Impact
Build AI solutions for a healthier planet and stronger communities.
Examples: climate, sustainability, agriculture, disaster response, smart cities, social impact.
Health, Wellness & Care
Build AI solutions that improve health, wellbeing, and quality of life.
Examples: healthcare, fitness, nutrition, mental wellness, elder care.
Education, Learning & Research
Build AI solutions that make learning, education, and research better.
Examples: tutoring, personalized learning, professional training, research, career development.
Business, Growth & Productivity
Build AI solutions that help businesses work smarter, grow faster, and operate better.
Examples: sales, marketing, CRM, analytics, productivity, automation, business operations.
Media, Entertainment & Creators
Build AI solutions for creativity, entertainment, and digital experiences.
Examples: film, music, gaming, content creation, creator tools, social media.
Commerce, Retail & Consumer
Build AI solutions that transform how people shop and how businesses sell.
Examples: e-commerce, marketplaces, retail, logistics, inventory, personalized shopping.
Build the Future
Whether you're creating a climate startup, an AI health company, an education platform, a new media studio, or an autonomous business operating system, the goal is the same:
Build a company where a team of AI agents can turn an idea into reality.
Come celebrate, build, experiment, and show us what the future of business looks like.
